renderer.background: transparent for measurement; radial dark-crimson canvas for the demo

crossSection.basis: a constant-thickness extrusion lands on 6-10 planes however many triangles it has; the previous pass had 29 separable meshes and every shell at 10, which passed every 2D gate and still read as cardboard

fixedView.basis: reproduces the supplied references' near-orthographic broadside product framing 1:1

referenceAdmission.detail: both views 2000x1125 RGBA with binary alpha, coverage 0.418/0.419, one enclosed hole (trigger guard), no duplicate: front vs mirrored back alpha IoU 0.9928 but mean |dRGB| 20.65 on the overlap, i.e. same silhouette / different surface

familyIdentity.detail: classified pistol/glock-18 at 0.94 from the GLOCK(18) roll-mark, the G18 breech engraving, the trigger-safety blade, the single right-side ejection port and the traced frame signature. Knife adapter explicitly NOT substituted.

silhouetteTier1.note: 0.9834, down from 0.9855, and the loss is a correction: the traced guard hole used to wrap AROUND the trigger, so the frame carried a solid trigger-shaped tongue that padded the silhouette. The tongue is gone and the real trigger module fills that space instead.

projectionCoverage.detail: every projected part (slide, frame, magazine, the serration and grip ribs, extractor, slide stop, magazine catch) shares one planar XY UV frame derived from the texture crop; the grip side panels are gone, folded into the frame as a plateau in its thickness field; the serration and grip ribs are parented to the shell they sit on and flagged explodeWithParent, so the exploded view moves them with their part instead of scattering them as loose slivers

paintedRegionParity.notes: port moved -10.2 -> -16.3 when the slide underside was opened, which changes what the transmission pass sees through the slide; the committed pre-loft build measured -14.1 there. Lightening the raceway behind the port moved it 0.1, so the channel colour is not the cause.
paintedRegionParity.regressionsFromPreviousPass: slideRear +0.3 -> +6.2 and guardBar +2.6 -> +10.6. Both are sloped cap surfaces the loft introduced and the flat build did not have, and both were measured down from far worse (+23 and +19) by scaling the slope to what the broadside gate supports. port -14.1 -> -10.2 and magExtension -9.8 -> +5.7 improved. Every front zone is now inside +-10.6.

slideSilhouetteAndPartingLine.basis: alpha trace; parting line measured as the darkest seam row (y=221) across x 350..1250

triggerGuardLoopAndHole.basis: hole is a real through-hole, traced contour, verified transparent (mean alpha 1.7/255 inside the bay)

gripRakeAndErgonomics.basis: alpha trace including the beavertail overhang and the backstrap undercut

decalPlacement.basis: GHOST / (*) / PROTOCOL / GLOCK(18) / G18 / >_ all carried by the projection, so placement is the reference's own

sightsAndTrigger.basis: rear-sight block and front-sight blade measured off the silhouette top profile; trigger's finger edge traced, its forked tail authored from both views; the safety-blade split is only faintly resolved (confidence 0.62)

translucentPolymerResponse.basis: transmission 0.3 / ior 1.52 / attenuated thickness, with real internals behind it; the back slide is the weakest zone

multiAngleForm.detail: no degenerate view. Top-down is a filled rectangle because a pistol seen from directly above IS a rectangle; the 70 px width is the real Z volume (a flat plane would collapse to ~0).

assemblability.slideRaceway: the slide is no longer a solid billet the barrel intersects: its traced underside is one full-length edge, and dropping that wall opens the U-channel a slide actually is. An inner raceway surface (back-faces-only) and two rail ledges close the mouth to the correct width.
assemblability.magwell: NOT cut. The mechanism exists and the grip base would open cleanly, but the cavity surface has to stay contained inside a translucent shell of varying thickness and does not — back-faces-only it still ghosts through the grip as a grey slab, which is visibly worse. The magazine tube occupies the magwell volume and reads through the polymer; the mouth is only seen from directly underneath, which no framing in this demo uses. Recorded as an approximation, not as done.
assemblability.triggerGroup: Safe Action modelled as two intersecting components: the shoe carries a through-slot at the traced safety footprint and the safety lever sits in it, thin and recessed at the pivot and swelling proud of the shoe faces at the tip. Shoe and lever use a dedicated matte grey polymer (roughness 0.7, metalness 0.1), distinct from both the translucent frame and the black polymer of the sights; the bar and connector stay steel, which is what they are. Lever, bar and connector are parented to the shoe and flagged explodeWithParent, so disassembly lifts the whole module clear of the frame in one piece.
assemblability.triggerApproximation: On a real Glock the safety lever sits in a notch that OPENS through the shoe’s finger face; here it is a closed through-slot, because opening an edge notch needs a boolean the loft cannot do. The traced blade footprint is interior to the shoe anyway (confidence 0.62).
assemblability.triggerTongue: FIXED AT SOURCE. The trigger is opaque in the reference and joins the frame at the top, so a plain trace of the enclosed void produced a guard hole that wrapped around it — the frame kept a trigger-shaped tongue at full receiver thickness and the build carried TWO triggers, the tongue and the real shoe on top of it. build_geo.py now punches the trigger footprint out of the mask before tracing the hole: 114 pts -> 75, top extended 0.356 -> 0.384 (the slot the trigger passes through). Every other field in geo.json is byte-identical. Verified by rendering the frame alone with a flat unlit material — the tongue is gone.
assemblability.muzzleBore: FIXED. The slide is a loft swept along Z, so its muzzle end is a WALL, not a cap: the nose was solid and capped the bore. Exploded you could see down the barrel, assembled the slide sealed it. The nose wall is now opened over the barrel span and closed by a muzzleFace plate carrying a round bore hole. Verified by raycast down the bore axis from outside the muzzle: previously the first hit was slide@1.708, now the ray reaches breechFace@-0.138, which is where a real bore stops.

approximations: Z thickness for every part is inferred from published Glock-18 cross-sections scaled by the traced height; neither supplied view resolves depth
barrel, recoil rod, breech body, magazine body and the ribbon-cable module are placed from what the translucent shell reveals plus mechanism knowledge, not from measured depth
the rolled-rim colour is authored (0x3a0710); neither view resolves the edge band

slide serrations, accessory-rail slots, magazine serrations and the grip stria are normal/AO relief rather than cut geometry — they do not alter the silhouette on a real Glock either, but they will not self-shadow at grazing angles
de-lighting is an approximation: the polished magwell specular streak and the slide's top gloss line remain baked into the projected albedo
the 'Well-Worn' float is a user-supplied label, not measured; wear is reproduced as the reference shows it, not sampled from a float value
notRun: object-sculpt-spec.json / validate_sculpt_spec --strict-quality / orchestrate_passes / append_review: this build went straight from the traced geometry contract (geo.json) to the factory, the way the shipped classic-fade demo is laid out. The gates were executed directly instead (admission, Tier-1 IoU, per-zone colour parity, multi-angle form, comparison sheets) and are recorded above.
divine_eye.py / vlm_gate.py were not invoked; scoring here is measured (IoU, per-zone RGB) plus the author's visual review of the comparison sheets.
actionRationale: Silhouette agreement is 0.986/0.986 IoU against both references, no critical feature failed, and the form holds from five non-degenerate angles. The two open items — the back slide reading ~15 counts dark and the ejection port ~14 counts dark — are material-response deltas on an otherwise matching build, and are refine-code work, not a spec or evidence problem.
